reason: council-remediation-2026-07-20/agent-P override of prior batch-070 source-scope retrenchment. The currently linked question's marked-correct option B and rationale claim 'PD 1067 specifies 20m easement for rivers >=6m wide' - this is FABRICATED. PD 1067 Article 51 sets easements by LAND CLASSIFICATION (3m urban, 20m agricultural, 40m forest), NOT by river width. The article body of lea-plan-004-02 only says easements 'depend on urban, agricultural, or forest context'. Council pass restores the original learning objective using the verified statutory rule.

source_audit_support.source_locator: PD 1067 Article 51. Article body lea-plan-004-02 normalized.md: easement widths 'depending on urban, agricultural, or forest context.' External verification via Lawphil and Supreme Court E-Library confirms Article 51 uses LAND CLASSIFICATION, not river width.

external_sources.citation: PD 1067 (Water Code of the Philippines), Article 51

proposed.text: A residential development is planned for a barangay that borders a river. The site is in an AGRICULTURAL area. Under PD 1067 (Water Code of the Philippines), Article 51, what public-use easement applies along the river bank, and what may not be built within that zone?

options.text: 3-meter easement; no permanent structures of any kind may be built within the zone.
20-meter easement; no permanent structures of any kind may be built within the zone.
40-meter easement; the entire zone must be fenced off from any public access.
No easement applies because the river is less than 10 meters wide.

rationale.a: Wrong. 3 meters is the easement in URBAN areas, not agricultural.
rationale.b: Correct. PD 1067 Article 51 establishes a 20-meter public-use easement in AGRICULTURAL areas along banks of rivers and streams (and shores of seas and lakes). The same article prohibits building structures of any kind within the zone.
rationale.c: Wrong. 40 meters applies only in FOREST areas, not agricultural. Fencing-off public access is not required; the easement is for public use (recreation, navigation, flotage, fishing, salvage).
rationale.d: Wrong. PD 1067 Article 51 does not condition the easement on river width; it is conditioned on land classification (urban/agricultural/forest).
rationale.correct: PD 1067 Article 51: along banks of rivers and streams and shores of seas and lakes, the public-use easement is 3 m in urban areas, 20 m in agricultural areas, and 40 m in forest areas. For an agricultural-area river, the easement is 20 meters and no structures may be built within it.
rationale.takeaway: PD 1067 easements are determined by LAND CLASSIFICATION, not by water-body width. Site planners must check whether the site is urban, agricultural, or forest before applying the 3/20/40 m rule.

proposed.explanation: Article body: easement widths 'depending on urban, agricultural, or forest context.' External verification confirms Article 51 uses land classification.
